name: Osteofibrous Dysplasia
aliases: Osteofibrous Dysplasia of Tibia and Fibula

criteria.description: Lesion localized predominantly in the anterior midshaft of the tibia and occasionally fibula
Presence of fibro-osseous tissue with irregular woven bone trabeculae rimmed by osteoblasts without malignant features
Onset in early childhood or adolescence
No evidence of malignancy or aggressive behavior on imaging or biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiographic lesion in tibia/fibula with characteristic histopathology and absence of malignancy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, radiological, and histopathological findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior tibial cortical thickening with fusiform swelling
pathognomonic.notes: Typically painless swelling localized to the tibia
searchTerms: thickened front shin bone with swelling

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fibro-osseous lesion confined to tibial diaphysis
searchTerms: fibrous and bony lesion in shin bone
swelling at front of lower leg

common.symptomName: Mild limb deformity (anterolateral bowing of tibia)
searchTerms: slight outward curve of shin bone

common.symptomName: Slowly progressive enlargement of affected bone

occasional.symptomName: Mild localized tenderness over lesion site

searchTerms: broken shin bone from weak area

occasional.symptomName: Limp or altered gait due to deformity
Fibular involvement with similar lesion characteristics

rare.symptomName: Pain at lesion site without fracture
searchTerms: pain at bone lesion without break

rare.symptomName: Soft tissue mass adjacent to bone lesion
searchTerms: soft tissue lump next to bone lesion
tumor-like soft tissue swelling near bone

rare.symptomName: Neurovascular compromise due to mass effect

laboratory: Normal serum calcium, phosphate, and alkaline phosphatase levels
imaging: Radiographs showing intracortical, expansile, lytic lesion with sclerotic margins in anterior tibial cortex
CT scan demonstrating well-demarcated fibro-osseous lesion without periosteal reaction
MRI showing low to intermediate signal intensity lesion on T1 and heterogeneous signal on T2
other: Histopathology revealing irregular woven bone trabeculae rimmed by osteoblasts within fibrous stroma

distinguishingFeatures: Fibrous dysplasia typically involves medullary cavity rather than cortex
Lack of osteoblastic rimming in fibrous dysplasia
More common in craniofacial bones and long bones other than tibia
Adamantinoma presents with aggressive radiographic features and soft tissue mass
Histology shows epithelial cell nests unlike OFD
Occurs in older age group compared to OFD

redFlags: Severe localized pain or night pain
references: Campanacci M, et al. Osteofibrous dysplasia of the tibia and fibula: clinical and radiographic features. Skeletal Radiol. 1980.
Schajowicz F, et al. Osteofibrous dysplasia: a clinicopathologic study of 59 cases. Cancer. 1976.
